reason: 2.1.1 declares --femto-font-size: 0.875em on small, but no rule applies it: only html, :host and h1 to h6 set font-size: var(--femto-font-size). So small keeps the browser's font-size: smaller, the parent size divided by 1.2 (0.8333em: 13.33px under 16px text, 14.17px under 17px). Pico 1.5.13 had small { font-size: var(--font-size) }; 2.0.0 kept the token and lost that rule. femto applies the token in content/typography.css, so small is 0.875em of its parent (14px under 16px text, 14.875px under 17px), 5% larger than in 2.1.1, and its line-height and the em-based sizes of its descendants, such as a code element, grow with it. A small nested in another small or inside a heading compounds as it did with smaller, and the hgroup subtitle rule (1rem) still wins. An author rule that sets small's font-size and loads before femto, or sits in a cascade layer while femto is unlayered, now loses to femto's rule, where it used to beat the browser's smaller; setting --femto-font-size on small now takes effect.
